name: Doxy.me vs Zoom for Healthcare
title: Doxy.me vs Zoom for Healthcare: Telehealth Comparison (2026)
description: Compare Doxy.me and Zoom for Healthcare for HIPAA-compliant telehealth. See differences in pricing, BAA availability, patient experience, and which platform is best for your therapy practice.

summary.bottom_line: Doxy.me is purpose-built for telemedicine with a free HIPAA-compliant tier, browser-based access (no downloads), and built-in waiting room—ideal for solo therapists and small practices. Zoom for Healthcare offers enterprise reliability and features but costs more and requires patient downloads. Most small therapy practices should start with Doxy.me.

key_differences.patient_downloads: Doxy.me (no, browser-based) vs Zoom (yes, app required)

sections.heading: Doxy.me vs Zoom for Healthcare: Overview
sections.content: Doxy.me and Zoom for Healthcare are both HIPAA-compliant telehealth platforms, but they serve different market segments. Doxy.me is purpose-built for telemedicine with a free tier that includes a BAA—making it the cheapest true HIPAA-compliant telehealth option. Zoom for Healthcare leverages Zoom's enterprise video infrastructure with healthcare-specific features. Important: Standard Zoom plans do NOT include a HIPAA BAA—only Zoom for Healthcare does. The COVID-era enforcement discretion has ended, so full HIPAA compliance is required.

sections.heading: Pricing & BAA Availability
sections.content: Doxy.me's free tier includes unlimited 1:1 sessions with a BAA—this is unmatched in the market. Paid plans ($35/mo Pro, $50/mo Clinic) add group sessions and custom branding. Zoom for Healthcare requires enterprise pricing (contact sales) and is expensive for solo practitioners. For individual therapists just starting telehealth, Doxy.me's free plan provides everything needed at zero cost.

sections.heading: Patient Experience
sections.content: Doxy.me has a significant advantage in patient accessibility. Sessions run entirely in the browser—patients click a link and join without downloading anything. This eliminates common technical barriers, especially important for elderly patients or those with limited tech experience. Zoom requires patients to download the Zoom app, which can cause friction and troubleshooting. For practices where patient tech literacy varies, Doxy.me's browser-based approach reduces no-shows and session delays.

sections.heading: Connection Reliability
sections.content: Zoom has the edge in connection reliability. Its enterprise infrastructure handles high-volume usage without issues that occasionally plague smaller platforms. Some Doxy.me users report connection instability—Trustpilot reviews describe sessions abandoned on Doxy.me and finished on Zoom. Doxy.me can also have issues when patients switch apps on mobile. For practices where connection reliability is critical, Zoom's infrastructure advantage matters.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Match the platform to your practice needs:

recommendations.when: You're a solo therapist or small practice, you want to start telehealth with zero cost, your patients vary in tech literacy (browser-based = easier), or you don't need enterprise features like recording and extensive EHR integrations

You're part of a larger healthcare organization, connection reliability is critical for your practice, your staff is already familiar with Zoom, or you need breakout rooms for group therapy, session recording, and deep EHR integrations
Your EHR (SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, etc.) includes telehealth—using one platform simplifies workflows and avoids juggling multiple systems

The COVID-era enforcement discretion has ended, so using regular Zoom for therapy sessions creates compliance risk.

faqs.q: Is Doxy.me really free and HIPAA compliant?
faqs.a: Yes. Doxy.me's free tier includes unlimited 1:1 video sessions with a Business Associate Agreement (BAA), making it the cheapest true HIPAA-compliant telehealth option. Paid plans add features like group sessions and custom branding but aren't required for basic compliant telehealth.

faqs.q: Do patients need to download anything for Doxy.me?
faqs.a: No. Doxy.me runs entirely in the web browser. Patients simply click a link and join—no app download required. This is a significant advantage over Zoom, which requires the Zoom app, especially for patients with limited tech experience.

faqs.q: Which has better video quality: Doxy.me or Zoom?
faqs.a: Zoom generally has more reliable video quality due to its enterprise infrastructure. Some Doxy.me users report occasional connection issues. However, for most therapy sessions, Doxy.me's quality is sufficient, and its ease of use for patients often outweighs Zoom's reliability advantage for small practices.
